environment: Linux CPU; Python 3.12.13; faster-whisper 1.2.1; CTranslate2 4.8.2; Torch 2.8.0+cpu; Silero 6.0.0; FFmpeg 6.1.1; four Torch/OMP/MKL threads

sources.fleurs: FluidInference/fleurs-full@1cca811bb8ea4d370345f108f00518167040282c; Google FLEURS, CC BY 4.0; attribution in speech-quality.md
sources.film: Tears of Steel — (CC) Blender Foundation | mango.blender.org, CC BY 3.0; 18–70 s excerpt; source https://media.xiph.org/tearsofsteel/tears_of_steel_1080p.webm

method.preparation: Same black H.264/AAC wrapper. Mixed cases retain source silence and append 0.5/3 s after ja0000,en0000,ja0001. No repeated sentence inside a case.
method.timing: Adapter wall time including audio decode, VAD and model load; excludes worker import/startup; one serial run per mode/case.
method.resume: Fresh process receives first completed production-format span; compare remaining output and final complete parts/cues. This run does not re-test database crash recovery.
method.text_comparison: NFKC, casefold, alphanumeric characters, Levenshtein; reference_edits means legacy,spans,reference_characters.
method.translation: Only compare translation input unit strings; no MT inference.

observation: Short-gap English VAD starts 1.716 s into source utterance versus 0.944 s with long gap; However missing in both short-gap ASR modes, present in both long-gap modes. Causation not isolated.
limits: Six short cases; no natural within-sentence code switching or 60+ minute dialogue.
Film compared with prior adapter, not independent spoken-word gold.
Punctuation/cue timing can differ despite equal normalized text; no word-alignment or translated-caption quality claim.
No new browser, Windows 11, RTX, peak-memory or throughput evidence.
